This evening through Sunday: Winds and cooling temperatures 
mark this period, with limited precipitation chances. A cold 
front continues to push east through the northern Rockies this 
evening. A deepening upper low drops in behind it tonight into 
Saturday; that low stretches as it shifts east, drawing a 
secondary backdoor cold front in from the northeast later 
Saturday into Sunday. This evening's front will continue to 
provide light precipitation chances over ID and southeast WA, as
well as near the Cascade crest. However these chances will be 
decreasing; by overnight the main potential lingers near the 
Cascade crest and the Camas Prairie, the Clearwaters and far 
southeast Shoshone county. 

Heading into Saturday precipitation chances are revitalized 
with the deepening upper low over the region. Chances start to 
re-emerge around the Cascades and far northeast WA and north ID 
in the morning, then chances start to expand from the Cascades 
through central and northeast WA and the ID Panhandle in the 
afternoon and evening. Overall the best chances are forecast 
around the axis of the trough, across the Cascades through the 
Okanogan Highlands with PoPs around 30-50%; PoPs elsewhere in 
the area outlined above are around 20%. I did go above the NBM
in the eastern areas of the CWA, where the northeast quadrant
of the low and instability could be enough to pop up a shower. 
Moisture is limited, so if something develops I don't think it 
will be much. Overnight into Sunday morning the precipitation 
potential retreats to lower Chelan and Douglas county, as well 
as southeast WA through the central ID Panhandle and wanes.

The lull in the winds tonight will allow for some fog risk over
the northeast WA and north and central ID valleys overnight/early
Saturday. 

* Snow levels and precipitation amounts: Snow levels this
  evening around 4.5-8kft, drop to 3.5-4.2kft by Saturday
  morning, moderating to 4.5 to 5kft Saturday afternoon before
  plunging to around 1.5-3.5kft by Sunday morning with the
  backdoor cold front coming in from the northeast, before
  moderating to 3.5-5kft Sunday afternoon. This will mean some
  mountain snow around the Cascades tonight, expanding into the
  northern WA and ID Saturday into Saturday night. Accumulations
  for the most part will be light, generally less than 1 inch;
  but some of the higher back-country mountains could see a bit
  more, up to 2 inches. Campers/hikers should be prepared for
  colder temperatures and that light snow potential. Heading
  into Saturday evening snow or a rain/snow mix could also be 
  found in some of the sheltered northeast valleys and overnight
  toward the central Panhandle to the higher Palouse. By Sunday
  the main light snow potential lingers over far southeast 
  Shoshone county. As for rain amounts, those look light. 
  Probabilities for precipitation amounts >=0.10 inches is 
  around 10-30% near the Cascade crest and central ID mountains 
  tonight. The risk increases some around the Cascades and 
  northern mountains Saturday afternoon and evening to around 
  20-50%. Elsewhere precipitation amounts are expected to be 
  less than 0.05 inches, if anything measures at all. Some may 
  not see any more than sprinkles.

* Winds/Blowing Dust: The winds will breezy this afternoon and
  early evening over the open basin, out of the west/southwest
  at 15-25 mph with gusts of 30-40 mph before then starts to
  wane after 7-8 PM. A blowing dust advisory remains in place
  for most of the Columbia basin to WA/ID border through 7 PM;
  several webcams around the region have shown visibility
  reduced due to blowing dust around the Upper Columbia Basin
  and Palouse and West Plains. Later this evening speeds decline
  to around 5-10 mph, with higher gusts to 20 mph, and less in
  the sheltered northeast valley. However, winds gradually turn
  north around the Okanogan Valley to western Basin, with speeds
  increasing there from mid-morning to afternoon with gusts of
  20-30 mph. Winds elsewhere Saturday will be lighter out of the
  southwest; however, by late afternoon and especially Saturday
  night the winds turn north to northeast through the region and
  speeds increase again, including this time much of north and
  central ID out through the Columbia Basin and continuing down
  the Okanogan Valley, with gusts of 20-40 mph possible. This
  continues through Sunday before decreasing later Sunday 
  evening into Monday morning. Additional blowing dust is in the
  forecast for Sunday to Sunday evening, with the highest risk 
  this time over the Upper Columbia Basin to Waterville 
  Plateau/Moses Lake Area. We will keep an eye on this for 
  impacts similar to today. 

Temperatures will be cooling over this period. Wind will impact
how cool some of the overnight readings get and in anticipation
of that I did go slightly milder than some of the NBM numbers 
for Saturday night/Sunday AM. Highs will be in the 50s to low 
60s this weeke
